To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The electrospun PVA/AgNPs/CMCS nanofiber membrane has good antibacterial activity against Gram (+ve) bacteria, (2) The antibacterial activity of PVA/Ag NPs/CMCS increased with increasing both CMCS mass ratio and Ag nanoparticles percent.
The antibacterial nanofibers can be fabricated by electrospinning of CMCS/AgNPs/PVA solution.
the prepared PVA (AgNP) CMCS nanofibrous membrane showed good antibacterial activity against Gram (+ve) bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of antibacterial composite from CMCS nanofibrous membrane containing AgNPs and PVA.
the synthesis of AgNPs and electrospun PVA/CMCS nanofiber mats.
the preparation, characterization and antibacterial activity of electrospun PVA/CMCS/AgNPs composite nanofibers for biomedical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prepared PVA (AgNP)/CMCS nanocomposite is a potential candidate as an antibacterial material for biomedical applications.
the antibacterial activities of the electrospun PVA nanofibers were enhanced by increasing both CMC and Ag nanoparticles percent.
the prepared nanofiber mats have potential applications in biomedical applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we prepared a novel antibacterial material by electrospinning of PVA (AgNP)/CMCS nanocomposites.
the AgNPs/CMCS nanofiber composite can be used as a potential antibacterial agent.
the Ag nanoparticles were prepared by chemical reduction method, and the Ag nanoparticles were incorporated into the electrospun CMCS nanofibrous membrane by electrospinning.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed an efficient, facile, and environmentally benign approach for the synthesis of Ag nanoparticles using carboxymethyl chitosan as both the reducing and capping agent and the electrospinning technique for the preparation of nanofibers.
we have successfully synthesized a composite of CMCS and AgNPs nanofibers by electrospinning technique and investigated their potential as antibacterial material.
electrospun nanocomposite fibers from carboxymethylichitosan (CMC)/Ag nanoparticles can be prepared by using poly (Vinyl Alcohol) (PVA).
